target_customer: Early: web publishers and players of Flash games; later: mobile game developers who pay for ads and promotion
problem: Game developers needed a way to distribute and monetize games across the web and then mobile apps, and players needed to discover games.
business_model: Ad network and cross promotion revenue (mobile ads, mediation), after an earlier free social games platform
product_category: Social games platform turned mobile ad network

founders.name: Immad Akhund
founders.background_notes: YC page: earlier founded Clickpass; later became CEO of Mercury

founders.name: Jude Gomila
founders.background_notes: YC page: later founded Golden, acquired by ComplyAdvantage in 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: A Flash game widget and distribution platform, later an SDK for iOS and Android with ad serving, which is standard engineering with scaling parts.

defensibility.rationale: Game discovery community and SDK footprint gave some scale, but ad networks and game platforms such as OpenFeint and Scoreloop were substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple added Game Center for iOS; Heyzap kept going, pivoted to ads and was bought by RNTS Media in 2016.

market_need_then: Flash games and social gaming were growing in 2009 with Ning and myYearbook hosting games, and mobile gaming then rose with smartphones; Heyzap reported 1.6 million users on its early platform.

branding.domain_note: Used heyzap.com; no purchase story found

rebrands.why: Fyber folded older brands including Heyzap and Inneractive into one brand per PocketGamer.biz

branding.community_and_virality: Badge based check in mechanic for games modeled on Foursquare and Gowalla per press coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Known in mobile game and ad circles but no evidence of consumer brand pull; the brand was later absorbed into Fyber.

pivots.to: Mobile game check in and discovery app
pivots.why: Move into mobile; date from a mirror source, unverified
Monetization via ads and mediation; exact date not found

outcome_analysis: Heyzap began in 2009 as a Flash games sharing platform, raised about 8 million in total from Union Square Ventures and later Qualcomm Ventures, and pivoted to a mobile ad network. Reports said it reached about 130 million users and was profitable in the second half of 2015 before RNTS Media, owner of Fyber, bought it for up to 45 million with a 20 million cash portion and earn outs.
notes: Competitor list left empty: no source dated around the January 2009 batch was found; the OpenFeint, Scoreloop and Game Center comparisons come from 2011 coverage. The 2010-06 round is stage other because the sources seen label it only as a 3M round led by USV (a weaker aggregator calls it Series A). Total raised sources conflict: about 8M (several outlets), CB Insights 8.08M, other aggregators 10M and 14.9M, treated as unverified. A 2009 seed listed by aggregators is unverified.
